messages.subject: I received my shipment but how should I proceed from here.
messages.text:
Hello,

I recently received my shipment of milkweed, but I am unsure how to proceed. I originally ordered seed bombs, but I received milkweed seeds in small bags instead (please see the attached photos).

I have reviewed the provided code information, but I still have several questions. Could you please provide guidance on the following:

 - Instructions on how and when to plant these seeds.
 - How to determine the seed count in each package.
 - Whether the seeds have already started germinating, as they appear to have begun the process.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,

MaryAnne Glasier

messages.subject: Re: I received my shipment but how should I proceed from here.
messages.text:
Hello MaryAnne, 

We sincerely thank you for your order and your interest in our products.

Due to a shipping issue, we have noticed that in some shipments, the seed bombs may begin to germinate before they arrive.
To ensure optimal quality and a better experience, our seed bombs are being replaced with our cold-stratified milkweed seeds, ready to sow: https://lasclay.com/en/products/cold-stratified-milkweed-seeds
 🌿 Same species as in the seed bombs
🌿 Easier germination thanks to stratification
🌿 Simple and straightforward to use
🌿 The price remains the same 🙂

 - Instructions on how and when to plant these seeds. 
 Seeds must be sown as soon as the package is received in order to preserve their germination potential.
 
 - How to determine the seed count in each package. 
 Each sachet contains 30 to 40 seeds as well as a substrate (sand)
 

 - Whether the seeds have already started germinating, as they appear to have begun the process. 
 Yes, the seeds were previously cold-stratified for 30 days.
 

 We remain at your disposal for any information; we’d be happy to help.

Thank you again for your trust, and we look forward to fully satisfying your needs.

 

 Warmly,
 __
 Hari 
 

 Lasclay

messages.subject: Re: I received my shipment but how should I proceed from here.
messages.text:
Hi MaryAnne,

Sorry for the delay getting back to you, the past few months have been extremely busy on our end and this one waited far longer than it should have.

That's genuinely disappointing to hear, especially since you followed the instructions carefully. Cold-stratified seeds should have a solid germination rate, so something clearly went wrong somewhere, whether with the seeds themselves or the conditions during shipping.

We want this to work for you, so we'll send you a replacement shipment of cold-stratified seeds. Is your shipping address still the same as on your original order? Once you confirm, we'll get them out to you.

A couple of quick questions that'll help the next batch have the best chance:
- Where did you plant them (outdoors in the ground, pots, etc.)?
- Roughly what temperatures were you seeing when you planted?

No rush on those, we can send the replacement regardless.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com

messages.subject: Re: I received my shipment but how should I proceed from here.
messages.text:
Gabriel, 
 I planted them in grow pots first as our spring weather was extremely cold and snowy. The temps were in the 20-30’s degrees F
 Then I transferred them outside under a porch once the weather started to warm up a little. (40-50’s) They never sprouted from that point on. I kept the pots moist with a spray mister as not to get them too wet then eventually put them out in the full elements (50’s- 70’s F). I eventually just dumped the seeds in the creek in my backyard since nothing was happening. (In July, 90 degrees) 
 Please let me know if I should have done something differently. Thank you. 
 My address is 
 6407 Meadowbrook Dr, Mentor OH 44060 
 If you want to wait again to send them in the spring after you do the cold-stratified storage over the winter, that would be fine also. If you can just let me know.
 
 If you could also just send a smaller amount of the milkweed that spreads as I don’t have as much area to plant it as I thought, that would be great. You could make up the difference with the swamp milkweed. Of course if this is possible. 
 

 Thank you again for helping me get this milkweed up and growing for the butterflies. I can’t wait to see some Monarch crystals’ ☺️
 Much appreciation, 
 MaryAnne Glasier

messages.subject: Re: My seeds
messages.text:
Hi MaryAnne,
 Thank you for taking the time to write all that out — and I am sorry it came to dumping the seeds in the creek. That is a fair reaction after everything.
 We promised you a replacement on July 15 and never sent it. That is the part I have no excuse for.
 We are refunding your order in full — $104.73. It goes back to the payment method you used; give it a few business days to appear on your statement. Nothing is required from you.
 You followed the instructions carefully, you adapted to a hard spring, and it still did not work. You should not be out of pocket for that on top of the wait.
 Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
